recipe.label: Gouache Poster

traits.medium: hand-painted gouache landscape poster with opaque matte color shapes
traits.texture: chalky matte paint, decisive brush edges and sparse dry-brush marks
traits.composition: simplify the garden into distinct depth layers; preserve the tree rhythm and path
traits.lighting: clear daylight described with flat light and shadow shapes

review_checks: tree rhythm and path survive simplification
limitations: A poster aesthetic does not supply print layouts or guarantee exact typography.
Palette and fine geometry are prompt guidance and require visual review across a series.

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: README style reference; intended use: One reviewed Gouache Poster example for the Art Skill style catalog
Primary request: A lush sloping hillside garden with a thick foreground tree trunk on the left, tall slender conifers across the center-right, dense layered foliage, distant bluish hills, a small blue roof lower-center, external stairs at far left and a curving path on the right beneath a bright cloudy sky.
Style/medium: hand-painted gouache landscape poster with opaque matte color shapes
Color palette: #F4E4BE, #426345, #759B62, #2F535D, #AFCAD0
Materials/textures: chalky matte paint, decisive brush edges and sparse dry-brush marks
Composition/framing: simplify the garden into distinct depth layers; preserve the tree rhythm and path; Keep landscape orientation and the original broad framing; one image, no frame or panels
Lighting/mood: clear daylight described with flat light and shadow shapes
Requested output target: 1536x1024, opaque background, png; use only supported tool controls
Avoid: real people; copyrighted characters; logos and brand marks; copied artworks; unrequested lettering
Constraints: Keep the original layered garden viewpoint, left tree trunk, tall conifer rhythm, slope, distant hills and curving path. Simplify minor details only to suit the medium. Do not add a sea, island bay, rainbow or sunset.; No added people, brands, characters, captions or signatures; Use only this source photograph as the composition reference; never mix motifs from the other photos
